You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

MAINTENANCE 11 Prerequisites Tool required: O TX10 key Procedure 1. Make sure that the environment is clean and clear of fog, moisture, and dust. 2. Check the effectiveness of the protective device. o Generally, the protective device is checked exactly as during commissioning. o If during the project planning the possible tolerances of the devices have been considered and it is ensured that the configuration, wiring, or alignment of the safety laser scanner have not been changed, a function check-out is sufficient. Complementary information In certain cases (in the event of dust, high air humidity), it may make sense not to disconnect the system plug and the safety laser scanner at first: 1. Move the safety laser scanner with the system plug to a clean location (e.g. office, maintenance areas). 4. Unscrew screws in the system plug and remove the system plug from the defective safety laser scanner. 5. See above for further steps. Further topics O "Replacing the system plug", page 114 O "Mounting the device", page 55 11.4.2 Replacing the safety laser scanner with system plug Procedure 1. Reconnect the connecting cables to the system plug. 5. Configure the safety laser scanner. 6. Perform commissioning again, taking particular care to conduct all of the thorough checks described. RIFERIMENTI NORMATIVI: L’obbligo di una corretta gestione delle attrezzature di lavoro è previsto dal Titolo III del D. Lgs. 81/08. (Testo Unico), articolo 71, in virtù del quale il datore di lavoro deve, non solo mettere a disposizione dei lavoratori attrezzature conformi ai requisiti di sicurezza, conformemente alle disposizioni legislative nazionali o di recepimento delle direttive comunitarie e adeguate al lavoro da svolgere ma deve anche provvedere affinché tali attrezzature siano oggetto di idonea manutenzione al fine di garantire nel tempo la rispondenza alle caratteristiche tecniche e di funzionamento originali. L’obbligo della manutenzione è applicabile a tutte le attrezzature di lavoro, nessuna esclusa. Per particolari attrezzature, il cui utilizzo comporta pericoli particolari e riportate nell’Allegato VII del T.U. e ss.mm.ii., occorre eseguire verifiche periodiche con una periodicità stabilita dal legislatore da parte di personale specializzato dell’ASP di competenza o Organismo privato riconosciuto. In appendice vengono riportati in forma integrale gli articoli 69, 70, 71 del D. Lgs. 81/08, nonché l’Allegato VII del medesimo decreto. Ogni attrezzatura e macchina dovrà essere sottoposta a un regime di verifiche e di manutenzione specifico, essenzialmente sulla base delle prescrizioni del fabbricante e di eventuali leggi specifiche, come ad esempio nel caso delle gru, dei trattori agricoli-forestali, delle piattaforme elevatrici, etc.. The safety laser scanner must detect the test object at each position and indicate the detection. How it is indicated depends on the configuration. The safety laser scanner must detect the test object at each position and indicate the detection. How it is indicated depends on the configuration.
